A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that mass spectrometry can be used for primary structure assessment, as well as to identify and quantify glycosylation patterns in mAbs.
we were able to establish the correct amino acid sequence and a complete glyco-profile for cetuximab and to show that the product has a homogeneous glycosylation profile.

we have developed a robust analytical workflow that allows the characterization of the amino acid sequence, post translational modifications, and glycoforms of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and their biosimilars.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mass spectrometry is a powerful tool for the assessment of antibody structure and post-translational modification profiles and can be applied for the development and characterization of biosimilars and for the establishment of reference standards for these products.

the combination of mass spectrometric approaches, including intact, middle-down and middle-up mass spectrometry, provides a robust and reliable tool to assess the primary structure and glyco-profiling for the characterization of mAbs.
the use of mass spectrometric techniques in the assessment of the structure and quality of biosimilars is essential to ensure that the biosimilar is truly comparable to the reference product.
